sourceNote: The mesh of the user with one local edit (assets/models/rhino/README.md, SHA-256 113b9ec65055a87b466d296fc53c5343bd7c130d7101c37dbc787a2b11b94a9d). The user said on 2026-10-22: "the panda and rhino's arms also got deformed". Each thick arm joins the trunk from the paw up to the shoulder, so the cut closed the inner side of each arm with one flat cap of 22 and 23 faces, which showed as a flat dark sheet when the forearm turned to the tuba. The copy removes the 48 and 49 faces that join each arm to the trunk below cut.top, and closes each arm with a round patch of 20 and 19 new vertices (docs/research/2026-10-22-rhino-arm/rhino_arms.py, docs/research/2026-10-22-rhino-arm.md). The hole of the trunk stays open, and the cut closes it.
name: Rhino

app.note: No reference image shows a rhino, so the mesh takes the head top of the parametric rhino (user, 2026-10-19, docs/decisions/2026-10-19-mouse-size.md): the standing head top of the parametric rhino with the tuba is 1.462 m (docs/research/2026-10-21-mesh-rhino/landmark-probe.txt). The skull top of the mesh between the ears is at 0.9415 u, so the scale is 1.5529 m for each unit, and the standing shoulder joints are at 0.575 u (0.892918 m). The reach is the reach of the arm factor below at that scale. With no --check, pnpm rig-mesh stops until the arm factor gives this reach.

armFactorNote: The factor of the upper arm and the forearm. The first config keeps the arms of the mesh: 0.431 m from the shoulder joint to the middle of the palm (check-first.log).
legFactorNote: The legs keep the length of the mesh (user rule: do not stretch the legs). The rhino stands to play the tuba, so no seat asks for longer legs.

upperTwist.note: The twist bone of each upper arm keeps 0.4 of the roll of the upper arm from the chest (StudioBody.upperTwist), the share of the hippo. With no twist bone, the skin of the left upper arm rolled 63 to 82 degrees at its largest step in the play of the tuba hold, above the limit 55 of the arm gate, for each elbow direction and left grip of the scan. With 0.4, it rolls 35 degrees, and with 0.6, 45 degrees (arm-twist.txt).

jointsNote: The places are in the units and the axes of the studio in the pose of the source: 1 unit from the soles to the tips of the ears, the soles at y = 0, +z forward, +x the left side. The right side mirrors the left side. The probes are in docs/research/2026-10-21-mesh-rhino/: sections.py gives the cuts at each height (sections-y.txt, sections-x.txt, sections-z.txt), and arm_cuts.py the cuts of the left arm (arm-cuts.txt, arm-cuts.webp). The rhino stands upright on short thick legs, apart below the crotch at y 0.17, with the middle of each leg cut at x 0.118 and z -0.07 to -0.1. The thigh joint lies a little below the crotch, the ankle at the narrowest leg cut, the knee halfway between them, and the toes at the ball of the foot (toe tips at z 0.029). The trunk joints lie about 0.01 behind the middle of the body cut (z -0.075). The head sits low and forward on a thick neck: the chin starts at y 0.69, and the neck joint lies below it. The skull top between the ears is at y 0.9415. The arm joins the side of the trunk from the shoulder down to y 0.35, with a notch at its front and its back (arm-cuts.webp). The middle of the arm cut gives its middle line: x 0.18 at y 0.53, 0.20 at y 0.47, 0.212 at y 0.41, and 0.216 at y 0.35. The shoulder joint lies on that line at the root of the arm, the elbow at y 0.45, the wrist at the narrowest cut above the paw, and the forearm twist halfway between the elbow and the wrist (upper arm 0.129 u, forearm 0.122 u, paw.txt). The finger joint lies at the root of the claws, and its tail at the tip of the paw. The ear joint lies at the root of the tall ear on the top of the head, and its tail at the ear tip. The thin tail hangs from its root on the back of the haunch (y 0.285) to the tuft at y 0.11. Each roll is the hint of the z axis of the bone, forward by default. The blunt paw has its flat bottom down, nearly along the forearm (paw.txt), so the arm bones take a palm that faces inward and back, as the palm of the hippo.

studio.note: The studio has no rhino. legTurns gives the world turn of each left leg bone from the seated bind pose to the source, and the right side mirrors it. The posture is the seated posture of design 5.2: the thigh slopes 25 degrees down from the hip to the knee, the thighs turn 15 degrees out, and the shin is vertical (docs/research/2026-10-16-hip-open/leg_turns.py <config> 25 15 0). The rhino stands to play the tuba in the app (the standing pose of the rig), so no player sits in this pose. The foot and the toes keep the turn of the source. The trunk shares and the bind arms are the values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, the wolf, and the monkey.

weights.armIslandsNote: The round patch of the inner side of each arm of rhino-arms.glb lies inside the turned plane of armFree, and only free arm vertices surround it. It follows the arm as the free arm does (arm_islands() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), as for the rabbit.
weights.armBelowNote: Inside the plane of the split, the share of the arm weight that a vertex of the trunk keeps grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height (source units). The cut frees the arm below 0.56, but bone heat gave the side of the trunk beside the forearm 0.14 to 0.21 of upper arm weight, and the arm forward at the tuba dragged it into dark slits. With the rule, the left crease share of pnpm arm-look falls from 15.7% to 13.9%. The ranges [0.45, 0.55] and [0.5, 0.56] gave 16.2% and 16.4% (docs/research/2026-10-22-rhino-arm.md).
weights.rigidNote: Each item takes the faces nearest to its points, and their corners take the mean of their weights (rigid_faces() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The first two items are thin faces of the inner forearm near the wrist, where the forearm, its twist bone, and the hand share the weight: the left face turned over in each sample and showed as a black facet under the forearm at az-150, and the right wrist folded three faces. The last two items are the long thin faces at the back of each arm root above the cut, which turned over in each sample (faces 38 and 2413 of the base). The middles come from pnpm fold-probe tubist --faces (docs/research/2026-10-22-rhino-arm.md).

armFree.note: The thick arm joins the side of the trunk from the shoulder down to the paw, with a notch at its front and its back (arm-cuts.webp). The plane of the split turns 17 degrees around the vertical, so that it passes through both notches: at y 0.42, the front notch is at x 0.150 and z 0.006, and the back notch at x 0.186 and z -0.10. A vertex of the free arm also lies within 0.085 u of the chain of the arm joints and above y 0.24, so that the side of the trunk below the arm and the top of the thigh under the paw are not a part of it (arm-free.txt, arm-free.webp).

sliver.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, the wolf, and the monkey.

line.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, the wolf, and the monkey.

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, so that the round haunch stays on the hips. It starts at the knee and ends at the thigh joint, as for the hippo.

weights.note: Beyond the turned plane of armSplit (armFree), only the free arm follows the arm bones: the part that holds the finger tip has 154 vertices from y 0.249 to 0.619 (arm-free.txt). Above headFrom, each vertex follows the head only: the chin starts at y 0.69. Each tall ear follows its ear bone above earBase, from its root at y 0.92. The thin tail is a ball on one bone (tailBall): the vertices within radius of the center and behind the plane z = behind follow the tail. clavicleFrom, armTop, and shoulderHead are the rules of the hippo, moved with the shoulder joint (y 0.575) and the neck of the rhino.

cut.lowNote: The copy rhino-arms.glb closes the arms, so the cut closes only the open hole of the trunk on each side (open_loop()). The hole reaches down to y 0.189, and the open edges of the tail lie below y 0.18, so the height low keeps them out of the loop.
cut.skinNormalsNote: The caps of the arm take the normals of the skin around them in the app, as for the hippo (docs/research/2026-10-19-cut-caps.md).
cut.note: The thick arm joins the side of the trunk along a seam from the paw up to the shoulder. Below the height top, 0.015 u below the shoulder joint, the faces with a corner in the free arm (armFree) and a corner in the body go, and new faces close the arm and the trunk, as for the hippo (docs/research/2026-10-18-panda-cut.md). With no cut, the seam faces stretched into dark spikes beside the belly when the arms moved forward to the tuba (lineup0.webp).

flip.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, the wolf, and the monkey.

refine.ringsNote: The first config has no rings. pnpm rig-mesh rhino --check lists the thin faces near the joints as candidates for a ring (check.thin). The fold probe of the role chooses the rings.

check.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, the wolf, and the monkey.

colors.note: The values of samples, palette, dark, and eyeShare are the values of the other meshes. A dark face in the eye box is a face of an eye: 8 faces on the right and 9 on the left, at |x| 0.053 to 0.067, y 0.81 to 0.83, and z 0.138 to 0.145 (colors.txt). The config has no nose box: the rhino has two nostrils and no nose pad, so the nostrils keep the skin color.

eyeShell.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, the wolf, and the monkey.

chair.note: The chair of the rig sets the seat top of the seated bind under the haunch. The rhino stands in the app (the standing pose of the rig, soloist of ANIMALS), so no player sits on this seat. The front edge lies behind the shins of the seated bind (from z -0.104 u, check-first.log). The other values are the values of the hippo.

crease.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, the panda, the hippo, the mouse, the pig, the wolf, and the monkey.

sit.note: The values of the hippo and the panda.
